intro: Searching for breast reduction near me usually means you're considering surgery to reduce the size and weight of your breasts, often because of back, neck or shoulder pain. You want to find a local cosmetic surgeon who can assess your situation and explain your options clearly. We introduce you to a suitable UK professional who can quote you directly, with prices on application.
need_heading: What people searching for breast reduction near me often need
need_lead: A breast reduction is a significant decision, and most people want to understand the practicalities before committing.
needs: You may be experiencing persistent back, neck or shoulder pain and want to know whether reducing breast size could help.
You might be unsure whether the NHS will fund your surgery and want to explore private options close to home.
You could be concerned about how surgery might affect breastfeeding in the future and need clear information.
You may want to understand what recovery involves and how much time you might need away from work or daily activities.
You might feel self-conscious about your breast size and want to discuss whether surgery is right for you with a local surgeon.
context_heading: What to understand about breast reduction surgery
context: Breast reduction surgery reduces breast size and weight, often to relieve back, neck and shoulder pain. It should be carried out by a surgeon on the GMC's specialist register, usually in plastic surgery or a related specialty, in a hospital or clinic registered with the CQC (or the equivalent regulator outside England). Many surgeons are members of BAAPS or BAPRAS, and the Royal College of Surgeons offers a cosmetic surgery certification.

The GMC requires doctors offering cosmetic interventions to give you time to reflect before agreeing to surgery and not to use high-pressure sales. Your consultation should be with the surgeon who will operate. NHS funding is limited, so it's worth discussing all options with your surgeon.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the symptoms you're experiencing, such as back, neck or shoulder pain, and how they affect your daily life.
Mention your general health and any existing medical conditions, as these can influence your suitability for surgery.
Say whether you're interested in NHS funding or private treatment, as this may affect the professional you're introduced to.
Explain your reasons for considering breast reduction, including any concerns about breastfeeding or future pregnancies.
Include your location and how far you're willing to travel to see a surgeon.
Note any previous breast surgeries or relevant medical history that the surgeon should know about.
questions: Are you on the GMC's specialist register in plastic surgery or a related specialty?
Is the hospital or clinic where you operate registered with the CQC or the equivalent regulator?
What does the consultation involve and will I see you, the surgeon who will operate?
What are the risks and complications of breast reduction surgery?
How might surgery affect breastfeeding and sensation in my breasts?
What is the recovery process and how long before I can return to normal activities?

faqs.q: Will the NHS fund my breast reduction?
faqs.a: NHS funding is limited and criteria vary by area. Your GP can advise on local eligibility, but many people consider private treatment if they don't meet the criteria.
Yes, surgery can affect your ability to breastfeed. It's important to discuss this with your surgeon, especially if you plan to have children in the future.
Recovery takes several weeks. You'll need to avoid strenuous activity for a period and may need time off work, so plan accordingly.

faqs.q: What should I expect at the consultation?
faqs.a: You should meet the surgeon who will operate, discuss your goals and medical history, and have time to ask questions. The surgeon should give you space to reflect before deciding.
